motion: Do we need God for morality?

items.currentText: Left the ultimate reason for an indifferent agent to value wellbeing explicitly conditional.
items.lockedProposition: Physical facts support a conditional prescription: if one cares about well-being, one ought not perform actions that demonstrably damage it.

items.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Dillahunty gives the abstract dispute concrete structure by connecting an acknowledged concern for wellbeing with physical facts that make oxygen deprivation predictably damaging and therefore action guiding. Principal limitation: The solution is explicitly conditional and consequently cannot obligate an agent who rejects the relevant concern which means it answers practical deliberation more completely than categorical normativity. Live burden: He must show either that morality needs no unconditional imperative or that the constitutive conditions of agency cooperation and vulnerability provide reasons even for agents who disclaim concern for others.
